title: Dedicated GPU pool autoscale warmup - debug breadcrumbs
content:
Quick breadcrumbs/notes around the recent dedicated GPU pool autoscale thrash and warmup issues. Notes to self + commands run and hypotheses.

Summary:
- Symptoms: repeated capacity thrash in dedicated-gpu-pool-prod-us-west, observed ~2025-10-30 02:00-06:00 UTC. Autoscaler repeatedly added GPU nodes, pods scheduled -> failed readiness/startup probe -> terminated/drained -> scale down -> repeat. Customer-facing latency spikes.
- Immediate mitigation taken: temporarily disabled aggressive burst policy for pool (policy=b0 -> policy=b1), set max-burst = 0, prevented further node churn.

Commands run (chronological):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gpu-prod -o wide
  -> saw many pods in ContainerCreating/Init
- kubectl describe pod <model-pod>
  -> Event: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503"
- kubectl logs <model-pod> -c model
  -> startup logs show model load: "loading weights shard 3/24" then long pause then "cudaErrorMemoryAllocation" in some cases
- kubectl logs <model-pod> -c init-warmup
  -> warmup loop: "prefill tokens=512 -> kv cache alloc 3.2G" then OOM occasionally
- kubectl get nodes -o wide && kubectl top nodes
  -> nodes created (p4d-24xlarge-like), initial gpu mem 0 -> sudden spike then pod eviction due to oom on node
- grep autoscaler logs (internal service): /var/log/dedicated-pool-scaler.log
  -> logs show scale_up decisions at t=02:03, scale_up complete at t=02:05, then scale_down request at t=02:08 (no traffic)
- system logs from node: dmesg show "Out Of Memory: Killed process" at same intervals

Observed error snippets: (copied)
- model container: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'"
- cuda: "cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory"
- startup probe: "/healthz returned 503"
- autoscaler: "node created but pods failed readiness -> considering scale down"

Hypotheses:
1) Warmup workload is heavy (full-model prefix warmup) and allocs large KV cache; multiple warmup pods on cold nodes cause OOM and kill each other -> autoscaler interprets short-lived failures as low utilization and scales down. Result: churn.
2) Readiness/startupProbe thresholds too aggressive. StartupProbe timeout too short for cold model load on our heavy quantized models (loads can take 30-90s). This leads to probe fail -> pod restart loop.
3) Node provisioning time vs. probe windows mismatch. Autoscaler sees nodes underutilized (pods not Ready) and triggers scale-down policies prematurely.
4) Device memory fragmentation or driver version mismatch on some node types causing intermittent cuda allocation failures. See two nodes with older driver (nvidia-driver 525.x) vs expected 535.x.
5) Scheduler binpacking issue: too many warmup replicas scheduled to same node (anti-affinity missing), causing node-level OOM while other nodes idle.

Quick diagnostics done / results:
- Replayed warmup locally with same image on a jupiter test GPU: observed 45-70s model load and ~3.4GiB KV allocations for long-context config.
- Checked node pool configuration: some nodes had mixed labels (gpu-type: a100 / p4d) accidentally, autoscaler mixes types -> variable load times.
- StartupProbe currently: initialDelaySeconds=10, periodSeconds=5, failureThreshold=6 -> 30s total -> too short for cold-start
- Liveness probe: tight interval as well -> we need to differentiate startup and steady-state.

Temporary fixes applied:
- Disabled burst scaling for pool (as above) to stop churn.
- Increased startupProbe failureThreshold to 20 (100s) for model deploys with large context; patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/618
- Added anti-affinity rule for warmup init pods (patch in k8s template) to spread warmups across nodes.
- Added node label enforcement to ensure only a single GPU type per pool (cleaner scheduling).

Longer-term action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Implement graceful warmup controller: 1) launch single warmup per node, 2) perform KV prefill more conservatively (prefill throttle), 3) report warmup progress to readiness endpoint so kubelet doesn't mark as failed.
- [ ] Add autoscaler policy tweak: respect 'startup grace' window after node creation (don't consider small period for scale-down).
- [ ] Fleet-level driver version enforcement + node image validation; add preflight check in scaledown path.
- [ ] Update model-serving image to stream partial readiness ("warmup_stage=1/4") and add startupProbe endpoint that reads warmup state.
- [ ] Create synthetic warmup-load metric to feed autoscaler (so autoscaler sees ongoing warmup CPU/GPU utilization).

Notes / follow-ups:
- Related Jira: OPS-4821 (tracking customer impact + RCA)
- Slack thread: #dedicated-gpu-pool-ops (link above)
- Owner for warmup controller prototype: Priya D. (Priya Desai)
- Next meeting: sync with SRE + infra on 2025-11-07 to land autoscaler changes.

Random scratchpad thoughts (brain dump):
- Could we use a lightweight sidecar that pre-allocs KV without loading full model weights? Might reduce memory pressure.
- Consider having a warmup-semaphore label: only N warmup pods across cluster at a time.
- For immediate patch, also bump the node-grace-period for pooled GPUs to 5m to avoid aggressive tear-down.

Who to ping: @Priya, @Miguel, @infra-oncall.

Commands to reproduce locally (dev):
- run warmup locally in container: docker run --gpus all -it redwood/model-serving:staging /bin/bash -c "python warmup.py --context 1024 --prefill 512"
- simulate probe: curl -v http://localhost:8080/healthz?warmup

End of breadcrumbs. Will keep appending logs & timelines here as I dig further.
